Biology Deep-Dive: TL1A / DR3 · IBD Pathophysiology · MOA Framework
What is TL1A and Why Does It Matter?
TL1A (TNF-like Ligand 1A, also called TNFSF15) is a cytokine belonging to the TNF superfamily. It is expressed primarily by vascular endothelial cells, monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells when those cells encounter inflammatory signals such as bacterial products, TLR ligands, or other cytokines. TL1A signals through its cognate receptor, Death Receptor 3 (DR3, TNFRSF25), which is constitutively expressed on T lymphocytes — particularly CD4+ effector T cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), and memory T cells. This constitutive expression means the system is "always ready" to respond, and even subtle TL1A upregulation in inflamed tissue will trigger T cell activation.
The key insight: TL1A is not just another inflammatory cytokine — it is a T cell co-stimulatory signal that amplifies responses to other activating stimuli. When IL-12 or IL-18 activates T cells, TL1A amplifies that signal 10–100x. In the context of IBD, where T cell dysfunction is central, TL1A acts as a "volume knob" for intestinal inflammation.
In the gut mucosa specifically, TL1A-DR3 signaling drives the expansion and activation of Th9, Th17, Th1, and ILC3 populations — the exact inflammatory cell subsets most relevant in both UC and CD. It also has a complex role in regulatory T cells: TL1A can both suppress Tregs (removing a brake on inflammation) or, in different contexts, promote Treg expansion — which is why patient selection and biomarker strategies are so important in TL1A drug development.
TL1A in IBD: Disease Biology
Multiple lines of evidence support TL1A as a causal driver in IBD, not merely a bystander:
Genetic evidence: GWAS have identified the TNFSF15 locus as one of the strongest genetic risk factors for Crohn's disease. The risk haplotype is associated with TL1A overexpression. ~60% of IBD patients carry a TNFSF15 risk variant — the basis for Merck's companion diagnostic strategy.
Expression data: TL1A protein is significantly upregulated in the inflamed mucosa of both UC and CD patients. Mucosal TL1A expression correlates with disease severity and histological inflammation scores.
Functional studies: TL1A-transgenic mice develop a Th2/Th9-driven colitis with small intestinal fibrosis — capturing fibrotic features of Crohn's disease often absent in other models.
Why this matters for BD: A target with strong genetic + expression + functional validation is significantly de-risked. TL1A has all three, which explains why multiple major pharma companies have committed billions in the space.
The TL1A × IL-23 Synergy — Why Bispecifics?
IL-23 (specifically the p19 subunit) is the master driver of Th17 and ILC3 differentiation in the gut. It promotes IL-17A, IL-17F, and IL-22 — cytokines that disrupt the epithelial barrier and sustain chronic inflammation in CD. IL-23 is already a validated target: risankizumab (Skyrizi) is approved for both CD and UC with strong efficacy data.
The key mechanistic connection: TL1A and IL-23 act on overlapping populations (DR3 is expressed on Th17 cells, ILC3s, and other IL-23-responsive cells) and co-stimulate in a synergistic, non-redundant fashion. Studies show that when both TL1A and IL-23 are present, the inflammatory response is greater than either alone — and that blocking one pathway leaves the other active to maintain inflammation.
BD Evaluation Lens: Why the Bispecific Premium?
The bispecific rationale: if dual blockade achieves meaningfully higher remission rates than either monoAb alone, a bispecific can command a premium label, pricing, and formulary position. The AbbVie TARGET-CD trial (risankizumab + trosunilimab combination, H2 2026 readout) is the most direct validation of this hypothesis. When evaluating bispecific programs, ask: (1) What are the expected additive vs. synergistic effects? (2) Which estimand design maximizes the detectable benefit? (3) Is there IND-stage efficacy data showing the bispecific outperforms both monoAbs?
IBD Drug Development: Endpoints, Estimands & Patient Selection
Endpoints: In UC, the standard primary endpoint for pivotal trials is clinical remission, defined by Mayo score. Composite remission requires both clinical and endoscopic remission. In CD, endoscopic response/remission and CDAI-based endpoints are used. Regulators increasingly prefer endoscopic endpoints as they reflect mucosal healing and predict long-term outcomes.
Why estimands matter: The composite estimand counts patients who required rescue medication as "treatment failures," creating a rigorous picture of drug performance in real-world use. Comparing tulisokibart (26.5%, composite) vs. duvakitug (48%, composite) requires confirming both trials defined composite remission identically — a 48% composite result is not the same as a 48% treatment-policy result.
Patient selection: Biologic-naive vs. biologic-experienced patients respond very differently to anti-TL1A agents. Companion diagnostics (TNFSF15 haplotype) can enrich for responders, but a more restrictive label limits commercial opportunity.

📐 Estimand Intelligence · ICH E9(R1)
Estimand Intelligence — Why the Same Endpoint Can Mean Different Things
ICH E9(R1) · Critical for interpreting IBD remission rates across TL1A trials
Essential BD Context ▼
An estimand defines the exact clinical question a trial is trying to answer — not just the endpoint, but how the trial handles real-world disruptions like rescue medication use, dose changes, discontinuations, and dropouts. Two IBD trials can both report "Week 52 remission" while answering fundamentally different questions. ICH E9(R1) (2019) requires sponsors to pre-specify the estimand before the trial starts.
Composite
Most common in IBD. Intercurrent events (rescue steroids, prohibited meds, discontinuation) are incorporated into the outcome — patients who need rescue are counted as non-responders. Measures real-world treatment success including tolerability. Industry standard for UC/CD Phase 2b/3.
Treatment Policy
ITT regardless of intercurrent events. All patients analyzed based on original assignment, whatever happened. Measures the drug's effect in practice. Can inflate apparent remission rates if patients got rescue.
Hypothetical
Ideal efficacy if the intercurrent event hadn't occurred. Estimates what remission would look like if no patient needed rescue. Useful for mechanism understanding but rarely used as primary estimand in late-stage IBD.
While on Treatment
Outcome measured only while patient stays on therapy. Excludes post-discontinuation outcomes. Underestimates real-world effectiveness for chronic diseases with high discontinuation.
BD read-through for IBD: When comparing TL1A remission rates across tulisokibart (Merck), duvakitug (Teva/Sanofi), and afimkibart (Roche), verify that all three are using a composite estimand with the same intercurrent event definition. A composite-based 35% remission rate is not comparable to a treatment-policy-based 45% remission rate. Future TL1A × IL-23p19 Phase 2 trials should pre-specify composite estimands to align with the emerging IBD standard.

  • Estimand alignment is a hidden risk in Phase 2 design for bispecifics. The three lead TL1A monotherapy programs in Phase 3 all use composite estimands. When TL1A×IL-23p19 bispecifics move into Phase 2, sponsors who use a different estimand strategy will report higher remission rates that cannot be compared to the Phase 3 monoAb benchmarks. Partners and regulators will scrutinize this.

Estimand Intelligence — TSLP × IL-33 Respiratory
ICH E9(R1) · Trial design & endpoint context
Essential BD Context▼
Respiratory trials use disease-specific primary endpoints that differ fundamentally from IBD. Asthma pivotal trials measure annualized exacerbation rate (AER) and pre-bronchodilator FEV₁; COPD trials add AECOPD rate, time-to-first-exacerbation, and St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ). Estimand choices affect how exacerbations during rescue steroid courses are counted and whether post-discontinuation events are included.
Rate-based AER (Asthma)
Standard for asthma pivotals. Negative binomial model of annualized exacerbation rate. Tezepelumab reduced AER by ~70% vs. placebo (NAVIGATOR). Pan-population vs. eosinophilic enrollment changes comparability across trials.
Time-to-first-event (COPD)
Used in tozorakimab OBERON/MIRANDA. Cox proportional hazards model. Clean handling of dropouts. If positive, establishes anti-ST2 in COPD with a registrational endpoint.
FEV₁ / Spirometry
Key secondary or co-primary in both asthma and COPD. Bispecifics may show greater FEV₁ improvement if both TSLP and IL-33 contribute to airway remodeling — important for COPD label differentiation claims.
Patient Stratification
Eosinophilic (eos ≥300 cells/μL) vs. pan-population analysis changes the apparent effect size. Tezepelumab's pan-population approval is the gold standard; restrict enrollment only if bispecific data suggest enrichment benefit.
BD read-through: Compare AER reductions only within the same population stratum. Tezepelumab's 70% AER reduction is in pan-population (NAVIGATOR). IL-5–targeting agents achieve similar reduction only in eos-high patients. Bispecifics entering Ph2 should pre-specify population and align estimand to maximize differentiation vs. tezepelumab.

TSLP × IL-33 / ST2 Axis · Biology Deep Dive
What is TSLP?
TSLP (Thymic Stromal Lymphopoietin) is an IL-7-related cytokine secreted by epithelial cells in the airway, skin, and gut in response to environmental triggers — allergens, pollutants, viruses. It signals through the TSLP receptor complex (TSLPR + IL-7Rα), activating dendritic cells, mast cells, basophils, and ILC2s. TSLP sits at the apex of the type 2 inflammatory cascade — blocking it upstream of IL-4/IL-13/IL-5 is why tezepelumab works pan-population, regardless of eosinophil count or IgE levels.
IL-33 / ST2 Axis — The Second Alarmin
IL-33 is an IL-1 family member stored preformed in the nucleus, released upon cell damage by allergen proteases or viral infection. It signals through ST2 (IL-1RL1), expressed on mast cells, ILC2s, Th2 cells, and eosinophils. Unlike TSLP (which primarily activates dendritic cells), IL-33 has direct effector cell activation — making them non-redundant. Blocking TSLP allows IL-33-driven ILC2 activation to persist, and vice versa. This is the mechanistic rationale for TSLP×IL-33 dual blockade.
COPD Biology — Why Alarmins Matter Beyond Asthma
COPD was historically a neutrophilic, non-type-2 disease. However, ex-smokers with eosinophilic features respond to IL-33 blockade (itepekimab AERIFY, 2025). IL-33 levels spike during viral AECOPD events, amplifying inflammatory cascades. TSLP upregulation occurs in COPD airways, particularly in ex-smokers with residual type-2 features. The dual alarmin hypothesis in COPD: blocking both TSLP and IL-33 could suppress both initiation and amplification phases of AECOPD, providing broader and more durable protection than either alone.

pH-engineered dupilumab backbone · Extended half-life · Reduced TMDD
Updated May 2026
May 2026
Dupilumab (Dupixent) ~$14.2B revenue in 2024 — defining the type 2 market ceiling Sanofi IR — Approved in AD, asthma, EoE, CRSwNP, prurigo nodularis, COPD (eosinophilic). Patent expiry approaching early 2030s creates biosimilar pressure and partnership urgency. Dupilumab's Q2W dosing and conjunctivitis risk (10–20% in AD) are the two exploitable gaps for a pH-engineered, extended-dosing successor molecule.
Apr 2026
Tezepelumab (Tezspire, AZ/Amgen) asthma Phase 3 DESTINATION 52-week data confirms durable exacerbation reduction NCT03078569 — ~70% exacerbation reduction maintained at 1 year in broad asthma population (no eosinophil threshold). Validates TSLP as a durable asthma target. AZ pursuing expansion into COPD (COURSE trial positive 2024). The IL-4Rα×TSLP bispecific directly competes with this approach — key differentiator is single molecule SC delivery addressing both upstream driver and downstream effector pathway.
Mar 2026
Ailux pH-engineered dupilumab backbone: key technical milestone achieved — AI-driven computational model solved the dual engineering challenge: (1) direct antigen repulsion at endosomal pH 5.5 via paired pH-sensitive residues within CDR and (2) CDR conformational shift to reduce affinity under acidic conditions. Result: antigen release in endosome → recycled antibody re-enters circulation without bound IL-4Rα → dramatically reduced TMDD, extended effective half-life. Patent filed as dupilumab composition-of-matter patent approaches expiry. This is the platform backbone for both IL-4Rα×TSLP and IL-4Rα×OX40L programs.
Feb 2026
APG279 (Apogee Biosciences): OX40L+IL-4Ra/IL-13 trispecific shows stat-sig efficacy in AD Phase 2 — Validates the concept of combining IL-4Rα blockade with upstream pathway modulators in a single molecule. Apogee also has APG808 (anti-OX40L) and APG990 (anti-IL-33). Apogee's multi-asset portfolio signals that the type 2 bispecific/multispecific space is heating up; first movers with differentiated platforms (pH engineering, half-life) will command premium deal terms.
Jan 2026
Dupilumab LIBERTY AD OAK/PRISM Phase 3: sustained remission data reinforces market leadership but dosing gap persists — Q2W dosing continues to be the primary patient-reported inconvenience vs. amlitelimab Q12W. The inability to extend dupilumab's dosing interval is a direct consequence of TMDD — Ailux's pH-engineered backbone is specifically designed to address this mechanism, potentially enabling Q4W or longer dosing with equivalent or superior IgG depletion depth.

🎯 BD Intelligence · IL-4Rα × TSLP Key Takeaways
BD Intelligence · Key Takeaways
May 2026
Actionable intelligence — Type 2 Inflammation / AD / Asthma
  • Dupilumab ($12B+ 2024) dominates IL-4Rα — differentiation requires explicit superiority. Any IL-4Rα-targeting bispecific must address why dual IL-4Rα+TSLP blockade outperforms dupilumab alone. The argument: TSLP blocks upstream initiation that dupilumab's downstream IL-4/IL-13 block cannot reach. If TSLP bypasses dupilumab's mechanism in a subset of patients, the bispecific captures a "dupilumab inadequate responder" label.
  • The bispecific design question: SC convenience + frequency. Dupilumab is Q2W SC; a TSLP×IL-4Rα bispecific with extended half-life could target Q4W or Q8W dosing — the single strongest commercial differentiation against a Q2W SOC. Biosion BSI-502 (TSLP×IL-4Rα, Ph1) is the closest comparable to benchmark against.
  • Atopic march creates multi-indication BD story. IL-4Rα and TSLP are both upstream of the atopic march (AD → asthma → food allergy). A single bispecific could target patients at risk of progression across all three indications — a much larger addressable market than any single indication.
  • Chinese TSLP×IL-4Rα programs are ahead. Biosion BSI-502 is in Phase 1, giving it a 2–3 year first-mover advantage. Partners evaluating IL-4Rα bispecifics will use BSI-502 Phase 1 data as a safety/PK baseline to compare against.

📐 Estimand Intelligence · IL-4Rα × TSLP Type 2 Trials
Estimand Intelligence — IL-4Rα × TSLP Type 2
ICH E9(R1) · Trial design & endpoint context
Essential BD Context▼
IL-4Rα and TSLP trials span two major indication clusters — atopic dermatitis (AD) and asthma — each with distinct primary endpoints. AD trials use EASI (Eczema Area and Severity Index), IGA (Investigator Global Assessment), and NRS itch score as co-primary or key secondary endpoints. Asthma trials use annualized exacerbation rate (AER) and FEV₁. ICH E9(R1) composite estimand design ensures patients requiring rescue medication are counted as treatment failures.
EASI / IGA (AD)
Primary in AD pivotals. EASI ≥75% reduction (EASI-75) is the registration threshold. Dupilumab SOLO trials achieved 36–38% IGA 0/1 at Week 16. Any new IL-4Rα bispecific must match or exceed this bar in a head-to-head or superiority design.
NRS Itch Score (AD)
Key secondary — reduction of ≥4 points in peak pruritus NRS. IL-31Rα pathway (nemolizumab) showed specific itch benefits; IL-4Rα blockade affects itch via IL-13-driven sensitization. Bispecific must address both itch and skin barrier dimensions.
AER (Asthma)
Standard for asthma pivotals (see TSLP tab). Adding IL-4Rα arm to a TSLP bispecific could show additive AER reduction in patients who have both eosinophilic and alarmin-driven disease.
Composite Estimand (Both)
Standard for both AD and asthma Ph3s: patients requiring rescue medication or systemic corticosteroids are counted as non-responders. Ensures real-world effectiveness is measured, not just per-protocol efficacy.
BD read-through: Compare EASI-75 and IGA 0/1 rates only between trials with the same rescue medication rules. Dupilumab SOLO used composite estimand; any bispecific trial must match this to support superiority claims. In asthma, AER reduction must be assessed in pan-population vs. eos-high strata separately.

IL-4Rα × TSLP Type 2 Inflammation · Biology Deep Dive
IL-4Rα Signaling — Why It Drives Type 2 Disease
IL-4Rα (IL-4 receptor alpha chain) is the shared receptor subunit for both IL-4 and IL-13 signaling. IL-4 signals through the type I receptor (IL-4Rα + γc chain) on lymphocytes, driving Th2 differentiation, IgE class switching, and GATA-3 expression. IL-13 signals through the type II receptor (IL-4Rα + IL-13Rα1) on epithelial cells, smooth muscle, and fibroblasts, driving mucus production, barrier dysfunction, and fibrosis. Dupilumab blocks both IL-4 and IL-13 by targeting IL-4Rα — which explains its breadth across AD, asthma, COPD, eosinophilic esophagitis, prurigo nodularis, CRSwNP, and alopecia areata.
TSLP Upstream of IL-4Rα Signaling
TSLP (Thymic Stromal Lymphopoietin) activates dendritic cells and ILC2s to produce IL-4, IL-5, IL-9, and IL-13 — the very cytokines downstream of IL-4Rα. Blocking TSLP alone eliminates the initiation signal; blocking IL-4Rα eliminates the effector response. Together, dual blockade theoretically prevents both initiation (TSLP) and downstream amplification (IL-4Rα), eliminating the most common escape route when only one is blocked.
Atopic March — The Multi-Indication Thesis
The atopic march describes the progression from atopic dermatitis in infancy → allergic rhinitis and food allergy in childhood → asthma in adolescence/adulthood. TSLP is elevated at every stage of this progression. IL-4Rα signaling drives each transition. A bispecific targeting both nodes could theoretically interrupt the march — preventing atopic progression in young patients — a much larger addressable market than treating established disease.

Actionable intelligence — Atopic Dermatitis
  • OX40L is a novel mechanism with first data incoming. Amlitelimab (Sanofi) is the lead anti-OX40L — Phase 3 OLYMPIA 1/2 data in 2025 showed ~47% IGA 0/1 responders at Week 16. This validates OX40L as a registrational-quality target in AD, directly motivating IL-4Rα×OX40L bispecific development.

  • Dupilumab loss of response creates partnering opportunity. ~20–30% of dupilumab patients experience secondary treatment failure or inadequate itch control. OX40L blockade in these patients (memory T cell re-sensitization hypothesis) is a specific, addressable BD angle.
  • AbbVie is a key competitive threat. AbbVie acquired Landos Biopharma and has OX40L programs; their combination strategy (ABBV-453 anti-OX40L + dupilumab-equivalent) is the most direct competitor to a bispecific IL-4Rα×OX40L approach.

📐 Estimand Intelligence · IL-4Rα × OX40L Atopic Dermatitis Trials
Estimand Intelligence — IL-4Rα × OX40L Atopic Dermatitis
ICH E9(R1) · Trial design & endpoint context
Essential BD Context▼
AD trials use EASI (Eczema Area and Severity Index), IGA (Investigator Global Assessment 0/1), and Peak Pruritus NRS as primary or co-primary endpoints. The ICH E9(R1) composite estimand is standard: patients requiring rescue topical corticosteroids or systemic treatments are counted as treatment failures. The composite estimand is essential for comparing bispecific data to dupilumab SOLO trial benchmarks (36–38% IGA 0/1 at Week 16).
EASI-75 / EASI-90
Gold standard in AD. ≥75% reduction from baseline EASI = "response"; ≥90% = "deep response." Dupilumab achieved 38% EASI-75 in SOLO-1 (composite estimand). Amlitelimab Ph3: ~47% IGA 0/1 — superior efficacy claim if confirmed in bispecific with same estimand.
IGA 0/1 (Clear/Almost Clear)
Co-primary with EASI in most AD pivotals. IGA 0/1 = clear or almost clear skin on 5-point scale. Dupilumab SOC: ~37–40% IGA 0/1 Week 16. Bispecific must show ≥40–45% to claim superiority.
Peak Pruritus NRS ≥4 reduction
Itch is the most patient-relevant AD symptom. NRS reduction of ≥4 points from baseline is the standard responder threshold. OX40L blockade may specifically improve this endpoint via memory Th2 cell suppression — watch for differential itch benefit in bispecific data.
Composite Estimand (Critical)
AD pivotals since ~2020 use composite estimand: rescue medication use = treatment failure. Dupilumab SOLO used this design. Any bispecific aiming for superiority claims must use the same design or specify why their estimand choice is appropriate.
BD read-through: Amlitelimab OX40L Ph3 used same EASI-75/IGA 0/1 endpoints as dupilumab. Any IL-4Rα×OX40L bispecific must match these endpoints to demonstrate superiority. Expect partners to require a head-to-head Phase 2 vs. dupilumab before a Phase 3 commitment — given the high commercial risk of launching vs. a $12B incumbent.

IL-4Rα × OX40L — AD Biology · Biology Deep Dive
OX40/OX40L Pathway — Memory T Cell Driver
OX40 (CD134, TNFRSF4) is expressed on activated T cells; OX40L (CD252, TNFSF4) is expressed on APCs (dendritic cells, B cells, mast cells). The OX40-OX40L interaction is critical for memory T cell survival and differentiation — it provides the co-stimulatory "third signal" that determines whether activated T cells become effector memory cells (persisting for years) or undergo clonal deletion. In AD, chronically inflamed skin generates memory Th2 cells that re-activate upon minimal allergen re-exposure. Blocking OX40L prevents this re-sensitization — theoretically enabling deeper and more durable remission than cytokine blockade alone.
IL-4Rα in AD — The Effector Driver
IL-4Rα drives the acute effector phase of AD: IL-4 promotes Th2 differentiation and IgE class switching; IL-13 directly disrupts the epidermal barrier (downregulates filaggrin, loricrin) and drives TSLP/IL-25 release — creating a self-perpetuating Th2 loop. Dupilumab's IL-4Rα blockade breaks this loop acutely. However, it does not address the memory T cell pool that was established before treatment — which may explain why some patients relapse when dupilumab is discontinued.
The Dual Block Hypothesis in AD
Combining OX40L blockade (memory suppression) with IL-4Rα blockade (effector suppression) theoretically addresses both the initiation of flares (memory re-activation) and the execution of inflammation (IL-4/IL-13 effector cytokines). The hypothesis predicts: (1) deeper short-term remission than either alone; (2) longer remission duration upon drug discontinuation (because the memory T cell pool is also being depleted). This is not proven clinically yet — the ZW171 IND filing and any bispecific Phase 1 data will be the first test of this hypothesis in humans.

Field Intelligence — IGF1R × TSHR · Thyroid Eye Disease
Dual receptor blockade · Orbital fibroblast pathology · Next-gen vs. teprotumumab
Updated May 2026
May 2026
Teprotumumab (Tepezza, Amgen) remains the only approved TED therapy — $1.9B+ annual revenue with significant unmet need Amgen — IV Q3W×8 infusion regimen, ~$200K per course. Key limitations: hearing loss/tinnitus in up to 30% of patients (dose-dependent), muscle cramps, hyperglycemia. Amgen acquired Horizon Therapeutics for $28B in Oct 2023 primarily for Tepezza. A SC formulation in development but mechanism/safety gaps remain. Hearing loss signal has prompted label updates and is the primary driver for next-gen development.
Apr 2026
FcRn inhibitor trials in TED paused/next-gen per clinical community positioning — IMVT-1402 designed for this space — Immunovant's IMVT-1402 listed as "designed to address" TED in Docs (2) with prior trial "paused/next gen." FcRn approach addresses autoantibody (TRAb) clearance but not the receptor-level pathology. The IGF1R×TSHR bispecific directly blocks the two co-activating receptors on orbital fibroblasts — a mechanistically distinct and more direct approach than IgG depletion via FcRn.
Feb 2026
Inebilizumab (Uplizna, Amgen) EQUAL Ph2 TED: B-cell depletion approach in moderate-to-severe TED — Anti-CD19 B-cell depleter being tested in TED based on the logic that TRAb-producing B cells/plasma cells drive pathology. Complementary to but different from receptor-level blockade. If inebilizumab shows effect, it strengthens the case that autoantibody reduction is sufficient — a tailwind for FcRn approaches but a potential competitive headwind for IGF1R×TSHR unless the dual receptor bispecific shows deeper or faster orbital response.
Oct 2025
Scientific validation: TSHR-IGF1R receptor cross-talk on orbital fibroblasts is required for TED pathology (Pritchard/Smith group) — IGF-1R and TSHR physically interact on orbital fibroblast cell surface; TSHR autoantibody (TRAb) stimulation activates IGF-1R signaling independently of IGF-1 ligand. This explains why teprotumumab (anti-IGF-1R alone) works, but also why its effect may be incomplete — TSHR continues to signal. Dual blockade is the mechanistic rationale for IGF1R×TSHR: block both co-receptors simultaneously to achieve more complete fibroblast inhibition.
Mar 2025
Teprotumumab OPTIC-X extension: sustained proptosis reduction at 2 years — but disease recurrence in ~40% of treated patients without maintenance — Sets the durability bar: ~40% relapse within 12–18 months of completing teprotumumab course creates a defined re-treatment need. A bispecific with SC administration and maintenance dosing option could address recurrence. Key BD framing: teprotumumab treats the acute episode; IGF1R×TSHR bispecific targets both the acute response and maintenance suppression of fibroblast activation.

📐 Estimand Intelligence · IGF1R × TSHR TED Trials
Estimand Intelligence — IGF1R × TSHR TED
ICH E9(R1) · Trial design & endpoint context
Essential BD Context▼
TED trials use highly disease-specific endpoints that combine ophthalmologic measurements with patient-reported outcomes. The primary regulatory endpoints are proptosis reduction (Hertel exophthalmometry, ≥2mm from baseline) and Clinical Activity Score (CAS) (7-point scale measuring inflammatory activity: pain, redness, chemosis, caruncle, lid swelling). These are combined in a proptosis responder definition. ICH E9(R1) composite estimand applies: patients requiring orbital decompression surgery or high-dose corticosteroids during the trial are counted as non-responders.
Proptosis Reduction (Hertel ≥2mm)
Primary registration endpoint. Teprotumumab OPTIC: ~52% achieved ≥2mm proptosis reduction vs. 21% placebo. This is the efficacy bar any next-gen TED drug must match or exceed. A bispecific claiming superiority needs ≥60% responder rate in a well-powered head-to-head.
Clinical Activity Score (CAS)
Secondary but clinically critical. CAS ≥3/7 = active TED; treatment is indicated. CAS response = ≥2-point reduction. Teprotumumab reduced CAS from ~5 to ~1.5 on average. Bispecific must match this; TSHR blockade may specifically address the inflammatory phase (CAS) by reducing TSH-receptor signaling.
Diplopia Reduction
Key secondary — degree of diplopia (Gorman scale 0–3). Proptosis causes mechanical strabismus → diplopia. Proptosis reduction typically improves diplopia. Watch for the TSHR arm's differential effect on orbital inflammation-driven vs. mechanical diplopia.
Hearing Safety Endpoint (Novel)
Critical differentiator for next-gen TED drugs. Audiometry (PTA) at regular intervals vs. teprotumumab historical comparator. If bispecific shows lower rate of ≥10dB hearing loss, this becomes a label advantage and key BD talking point.
BD read-through: Teprotumumab's 52% proptosis responder rate is the historical benchmark. Any bispecific must beat or match this AND show improved safety (hearing) to justify next-generation positioning. Regulators will likely require a dedicated hearing safety analysis in the IND-enabling package. The composite estimand must include orbital decompression surgery as a treatment failure event.

IGF1R × TSHR TED Biology · Biology Deep Dive
IGF1R in TED — The Orbital Fibroblast Driver
IGF-1R (Insulin-like Growth Factor 1 Receptor) is overexpressed on orbital fibroblasts in TED patients. Upon activation by IGF-1 (or by IGF-1R cross-activation from TSHR), orbital fibroblasts differentiate into myofibroblasts (causing fibrosis) or fibrocytes/hyalocytes that produce excessive hyaluronan and glycosaminoglycans — causing orbital tissue expansion and proptosis. Teprotumumab (anti-IGF-1R mAb) blocks this fibroblast activation, explaining its dramatic proptosis reduction in the OPTIC trial.
TSHR Cross-Talk — Why Bispecific?
TSHR (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone Receptor) is the autoimmune target in Graves' disease: anti-TSHR antibodies (TSAbs) stimulate TSHR on thyroid follicular cells (causing hyperthyroidism) and on orbital fibroblasts (causing TED). TSAbs acting on orbital fibroblast TSHR activate the IGF-1R signaling pathway through physical receptor cross-talk (TSHR and IGF-1R form a signaling complex on fibroblast membranes). Blocking TSHR removes the autoimmune stimulus; blocking IGF-1R prevents downstream fibroblast activation. A bispecific targeting both receptors eliminates both the trigger (TSHR) and the effector (IGF-1R) — a mechanistically complete approach.
Hearing Loss Risk — The Sensorineural Issue
Teprotumumab is associated with sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) in ~10–30% of patients (FDA label warning). The mechanism: IGF-1R is expressed on cochlear hair cells, which depend on IGF-1 for maintenance. IGF-1R blockade may impair cochlear hair cell survival. A bispecific that reduces the required anti-IGF-1R dose (by synergizing with TSHR blockade) could reduce SNHL risk. This is a clinically meaningful differentiator — hearing loss is the single biggest commercial limitation of teprotumumab and a key BD talking point.

🎯 BD Intelligence · FcRn Bispecific Key Takeaways
BD Intelligence · Key Takeaways
May 2026
Actionable intelligence — Autoimmune Neurology / IgG-mediated disease
  • FcRn is proven: efgartigimod (argenx), nipocalimab (J&J), rozanolixizumab (UCB) are all approved or late-stage. FcRn inhibitors reduce pathogenic IgG titers by 60–85% in gMG, CIDP, ITP, and multiple other IgG-mediated autoimmune diseases. The BD angle: what does a bispecific add over a monoAb FcRn inhibitor?
  • The bispecific thesis: FcRn + disease-specific second arm. argenx already has ARGX-117 (FcRn×CD131 bispecific targeting FcRn + eosinophilic disease signaling). The most promising rationale: FcRn×CD19 (B cell depletion + IgG recycling inhibition) for deeper and more durable remission in autoimmune diseases driven by pathogenic B cells.
  • Albumin sparing is the critical safety differentiator. First-gen FcRn inhibitors (batoclimab) had albumin loss — IMVT-1402 (Immunovant) redesigned for albumin sparing and is now in Phase 2/3 in multiple indications. A bispecific must maintain FcRn inhibition without albumin loss — this is the key design constraint.
  • Multiple indications are the BD story. gMG ($600M+ US market), CIDP ($1B+), ITP, pemphigus vulgaris, NMOSD, anti-NMDAR encephalitis — all IgG-mediated. A differentiated FcRn bispecific with clean safety could address 5–7 autoimmune indications off a single registration trial portfolio.

Ailux Positioning — FcRn Bispecific Autoimmune
Strategic Context vs. Field
Mechanism
FcRn + disease-specific second arm
FcRn inhibition depletes pathogenic IgG by 60–85%. Adding a disease-specific second arm (e.g., CD19 for B cell depletion) could achieve both IgG clearance AND long-term B cell suppression for durable remission.
Albumin Safety
Albumin-sparing design is mandatory
First-gen FcRn inhibitors had albumin loss. IMVT-1402 redesigned for albumin sparing. Any new FcRn bispecific must demonstrate albumin-sparing in pre-clinical and IND-enabling studies.
BD Opportunity
Multi-indication platform
FcRn mechanism applies to 5–7 IgG-mediated autoimmune diseases. A differentiated bispecific with clean safety profile can be sequentially registered across gMG → CIDP → ITP → pemphigus → NMOSD — each adding incremental value.

Estimand Intelligence — FcRn Bispecific Autoimmune
ICH E9(R1) · Trial design & endpoint context
Essential BD Context▼
FcRn inhibitor trials span multiple indications, each with disease-specific primary endpoints. In gMG (generalized myasthenia gravis): MG-ADL score (8-item Activities of Daily Living scale; responder = ≥3-point reduction) and QMG (Quantitative MG score). In CIDP: I-RODS (Inflammatory-Rasch-built Overall Disability Scale) and ONLS (Overall Neuropathy Limitations Scale). In ITP: platelet count ≥50 × 10⁹/L responder rate. ICH E9(R1) composite estimand: rescue IVIg use counts as treatment failure.
MG-ADL (gMG Primary)
≥3-point improvement from baseline = "responder." Efgartigimod ADAPT: 68% of MG-ADL-confirmed responders vs. 30% placebo. Nipocalimab VIVACITY-MG3: similar responder rates. Bispecific must achieve ≥65% MG-ADL responder rate to compete.
IgG Reduction Biomarker
Not a primary endpoint but essential for mechanism validation. FcRn inhibitors reduce total IgG by 60–85%. For IgG-mediated diseases (MG: anti-AChR IgG; CIDP: anti-paranodal IgG), the correlation between total IgG reduction and disease-specific antibody reduction is imperfect. Measure both total IgG AND disease-specific autoantibody titers.
Albumin Safety Endpoint
Serum albumin monitoring at scheduled intervals. IMVT-1402 redesigned specifically for albumin sparing. Any FcRn bispecific must include pre-specified albumin safety stopping rules and demonstrate comparable albumin preservation to IMVT-1402 benchmark.
CIDP I-RODS
Rasch-built functional disability scale (0–48). Primary in CIDP CADENCE trial (efgartigimod + NCS). Bispecific entering CIDP must use same scale for cross-trial comparisons.
BD read-through: FcRn inhibitor trials are now well-standardized around MG-ADL (gMG) and I-RODS (CIDP). Bispecific must pre-specify whether it aims to match or outperform FcRn monoAb benchmarks. The second arm's contribution must be measurable — specify biomarkers for both FcRn effect (IgG reduction) and second arm effect (B cell count for CD19; cytokine suppression for FcγRIIb).

FcRn (Neonatal Fc Receptor) Biology · Biology Deep Dive
How FcRn Works — The IgG Recycling Mechanism
FcRn (Neonatal Fc Receptor, also encoded by FCGRT) is expressed on endosomal membranes inside vascular endothelial cells and macrophages. Its primary function: prevent lysosomal degradation of IgG antibodies. When IgG is taken up by pinocytosis from circulation, it binds FcRn in the acidic endosome (pH 6.0), escapes degradation, and is recycled back to the cell surface where it's released at physiologic pH (7.4). Blocking FcRn prevents this recycling — IgG that enters the endosome is degraded, reducing total IgG half-life from ~21 days to ~3–5 days and circulating IgG levels by 60–85%.
Why IgG Reduction Treats Autoimmune Disease
In IgG-mediated autoimmune diseases (gMG: anti-AChR antibodies destroy neuromuscular junction; CIDP: anti-NF155/CASPR1/2 antibodies disrupt peripheral nerve nodal architecture; pemphigus vulgaris: anti-desmoglein antibodies destroy skin epithelial adhesion), pathogenic IgG autoantibodies are the direct disease driver. Reducing total IgG by 60–85% dilutes the pathogenic autoantibody titer proportionally. This is why FcRn inhibitors work across multiple unrelated autoimmune diseases — the mechanism is agnostic to the specific autoantibody target.
FcRn Bispecific Rationale — What Does a Second Arm Add?
FcRn monoAbs achieve IgG reduction but don't suppress the B cell source of autoantibodies. After treatment, autoantibody titers rebound when FcRn inhibitor is withdrawn. A bispecific adding B cell depletion (anti-CD19) addresses both IgG clearance AND long-term autoantibody source suppression — potentially enabling drug holidays or less frequent maintenance dosing. Albumin sparing: FcRn also recycles albumin; anti-FcRn antibodies that co-block albumin binding cause hypoalbuminemia. The engineering challenge is designing bispecifics that maintain selective IgG recycling blockade without albumin binding disruption.

Deal also includes CND261 (CD20×CD3, Ph1) and CND319 (CD19×CD20, preclinical). Transaction expected to close Q2/Q3 2026. Second major pharma validation of BCMAxCD19xCD3 format in autoimmune after Sanofi/HXN-1031 ($2.56B) — confirms that ≥$2B upfront is the market rate for preclinical trispecific B/plasma cell depletors. Mar 2026
Kali Therapeutics KT501 (CD19×BCMA×CD3): first patient dosed Phase 1a — March 18, 2026 Kali Therapeutics — IgG-like SC trispecific, "CD3 masking" platform to maximize potency and minimize CRS. Lead indication: Rheumatoid Arthritis. First direct competitor to ACE to reach the clinic. RA is defensible but arguably not the strongest immune reset story — SLE, myasthenia gravis, and SSc have stronger autoantibody-driven mechanistic rationale. Feb 2026
CLN-978 (Cullinan) CD19×CD3×HSA: Phase 1 OUTRACE trial — first data expected Q2 2026 Cullinan — 65 kDa small construct (SC favorable), attenuated CD3, two scFvs + anti-HSA nanobody. Phase 1 — most advanced CD19×CD3 bispecific in autoimmune (No DLTs at 10 or 20 μg; 30 μg enrolling). Active OUTRACE trials: SLE, RA, Sjögren's across US, Europe, Australia. Key limitation: only CD19 arm — misses plasma cell compartment (BCMA). ACE/full lineage depletion rationale: long-lived plasma cells in bone marrow are CD19−/BCMA+ — only BCMA arm reaches them.
2024
Three landmark papers in 2024 validate the immune reset hypothesis across three independent mechanisms — (1) Müller et al. (NEJM 2024): CD19 CAR-T in 15 SLE/SSc/myositis patients → complete remission, all immunosuppression stopped, drug-free months-to-years. (2) Bucci et al. (Nature Medicine 2024): blinatumomab (CD19×CD3) off-the-shelf → drug-free remission in refractory RA. (3) Alexander et al. (NEJM 2024): teclistamab (BCMA×CD3) → remission in refractory SLE. These three papers together make the ACE hypothesis almost axiomatic: if CD19 alone works (CAR-T, blinatumomab) AND BCMA alone works (teclistamab), a molecule targeting both should achieve deeper and more durable depletion.
2024
HXN-1031 (Helixon): CD19×BCMA×CD3 trispecific TCE — Sanofi-backed ($2.56B deal) — confirms big pharma conviction in the format — Pre-IND/pre-clinical stage. Sub-micromolar CD3 affinity (attenuated intentionally) to limit CRS risk. Published NHP data: depletion in peripheral blood AND bone marrow, sustained Ig reduction. Sanofi's decision to pay up to $2.56B for a pre-IND trispecific TCE is the strongest deal validation the ACE format has received — signals that commercial partners are convinced of the mechanism before clinical proof, which is exactly the window for ACE positioning.
Mar 2025
Excalipoint (Shanghai) raises $68.7M for trispecific TCE platform — China executing on the format at speed Fierce Biotech — EXP011 (CTM012): DLL3×CD3×4-1BB in Ph1 (SCLC). EXP012 (CTM013): CD3×4-1BB×CDH17 entering clinical 2025. Oncology-first but demonstrates Chinese biotech mastery of trispecific TCE format. Competitive pressure on ACE timelines — need to move quickly from preclinical to IND to be ahead of the next wave of China-sourced autoimmune TCEs.

🎯 BD Intelligence · BCMA × CD19 × CD3 Key Takeaways
BD Intelligence · Key Takeaways
May 2026
Actionable intelligence — Immune Reset / Autoimmune Hematology
  • CAR-T in autoimmune disease is the most disruptive BD story of 2023–2026. Kyverna, Cabaletta, BMS, Novartis are all racing to apply CD19 and BCMA-targeting cell therapies to severe autoimmune diseases (SLE, SSc, inflammatory myopathy, MG). First proof of concept: Fabian et al. (NEJM 2022) — 5/5 refractory SLE patients achieved drug-free remission at 2 years with CD19 CAR-T. This is a potentially curative one-time therapy story.
  • BCMA×CD19×CD3 trispecific is an "immune reset without bone marrow transplant" concept. Targeting both BCMA (long-lived plasma cells) and CD19 (B cell progenitors + mature B cells) depletes the entire B cell lineage that produces pathogenic autoantibodies. Adding CD3 co-stimulation redirects T cells to the kill. This is the most aggressive B cell depletion approach available outside of bone marrow transplant.
  • Regulatory path is being defined in real-time. There is no approved CAR-T for autoimmune disease yet. FDA is navigating a new framework for one-time potentially curative treatments in non-oncologic indications. The first approved product will set the precedent — BMS, Novartis, Kyverna, and Cabaletta are all racing for this position. First-mover advantage is enormous.
  • Manufacturing and access are major BD considerations. Autologous CAR-T requires apheresis, manufacturing (3–4 week turnaround), and lymphodepletion chemotherapy before infusion. Allogeneic (off-the-shelf) CAR-T would dramatically broaden access. Any trispecific antibody approach (vs. CAR-T) sidesteps manufacturing entirely — this is the Ailux "antibody engineering vs. cell therapy" differentiation angle.

🧬 Ailux Profile · BCMA × CD19 × CD3 Immune Reset
Ailux Positioning — BCMA × CD19 × CD3 Immune Reset
Strategic Context vs. Field
Platform Angle
Trispecific antibody vs. CAR-T
Ailux's antibody engineering platform can target BCMA + CD19 + CD3 in a single trispecific molecule — achieving the same B cell + plasma cell depletion as CAR-T without cell manufacturing, apheresis, or lymphodepletion. This is the "drug, not cell therapy" differentiation angle.
Commercial Advantage
Scalable manufacturing
An antibody trispecific can be manufactured at scale in commercial bioreactors — unlike autologous CAR-T which requires individual patient manufacturing. This dramatically broadens patient access and reduces cost-of-goods.
Target Patient Population
Severe, refractory autoimmune disease
SLE, SSc, inflammatory myopathy, refractory MG — patients who have failed 2+ standard lines of therapy and have life-threatening or organ-threatening disease. This is the "immune reset" population where the risk-benefit of aggressive B cell depletion is most favorable.
BD Partners
Autoimmune + hematology pharma
BMS, AbbVie, Roche, J&J, Novartis all have stakes in this space via CAR-T, B cell depletion, or autoimmune platforms. A differentiated trispecific antibody would attract BD interest as a next-generation alternative to CAR-T.

📐 Estimand Intelligence · BCMA × CD19 × CD3 Immune Reset Trials
Estimand Intelligence — BCMA × CD19 × CD3 Immune Reset
ICH E9(R1) · Trial design & endpoint context
Essential BD Context▼
Autoimmune immune reset trials use indication-specific primary endpoints but share common B-cell depletion biomarker endpoints that define mechanism. For SLE: SLEDAI-2K (SLE Disease Activity Index), BILAG, and the SRI-4 responder index (composite). For SSc: mRSS (modified Rodnan Skin Score) and FVC% predicted. For MG: MG-ADL and QMG score. All trials should include B cell reconstitution monitoring and autoantibody titer tracking.
SRI-4 Responder (SLE Primary)
Standard SLE registration endpoint. SRI-4 = SLEDAI-2K reduction ≥4 + no new BILAG A/B domain + no worsening of PGA. Anifrolumab (Saphnelo) SRI-4 rates ~47–55% vs. placebo 31–36%. Immune reset trials should show sustained SRI-4 response with drug-free follow-up — a paradigm shift from maintenance biologic dosing.
B Cell Depletion Kinetics (Biomarker)
CD19+ B cells, CD27+ memory B cells, CD19-/CD38+/CD138+ plasmablasts, and BCMA+ bone marrow plasma cells all measured at baseline, Week 2, 4, 12, 24, and during follow-up. The biomarker story defines the immune reset narrative — depth of depletion and speed of reconstitution predict remission durability.
Autoantibody Titer Reduction (Biomarker)
Anti-dsDNA (SLE), anti-topoisomerase (SSc), anti-MDA5 (myositis), anti-AChR (MG) measured at each timepoint. Titer reduction lags B cell depletion by weeks to months. Post-reconstitution titer: does it come back lower? This is the key question for "immune reset" — does the newly reconstituted immune system have a different (lower-autoimmunity) set point?
Composite Estimand / Drug-free Remission (Novel)
For immune reset, the key novel estimand is "drug-free remission at Month 12 or 24 post-treatment." This is a completely different estimand from standard autoimmune maintenance biologics. FDA has not standardized this for non-oncology indications. Sponsors must justify this endpoint in pre-IND meetings.
BD read-through: Immune reset trials require novel estimand strategies not yet standardized by regulators. The first company to achieve FDA-accepted drug-free remission endpoint in SLE or SSc will define the field. Partners evaluating trispecific antibody approaches need to see: (1) B cell depletion depth comparable to CAR-T benchmarks; (2) tolerability superior to CAR-T (no grade 3+ CRS); (3) manufacturing scalability. These three factors define the deal premium.

BCMA × CD19 × CD3 — B Cell Immune Reset · Biology Deep Dive
Why BCMA + CD19 + CD3 for Immune Reset?
CD19 is expressed on all mature B cells from pre-B cells through plasmablasts — including the B cells that are activated by autoantigens and produce pathogenic autoantibodies. Depleting CD19+ cells eliminates the "recent" autoantibody-producing population. BCMA (B Cell Maturation Antigen, TNFRSF17) is expressed on long-lived plasma cells in the bone marrow — the cells that were established years or decades ago and continuously produce autoantibodies even after CD19+ B cell depletion. Combining anti-BCMA (plasma cell depletion) with anti-CD19 (mature B cell depletion) addresses both the existing autoantibody reservoir and the ongoing B cell activation. CD3 engagement recruits cytotoxic T cells (CTLs) to kill the B cell/plasma cell targets — the same mechanism as bispecific T cell engagers (BiTEs) in oncology, now applied to autoimmune.
Why CAR-T Works — And What Antibodies May Match
CD19 CAR-T in refractory SLE achieves 90–99% peripheral B cell depletion within 1–2 weeks, followed by bone marrow plasma cell depletion. The Erlangen group showed 5/5 refractory SLE patients achieved drug-free remission at 2 years after CD19 CAR-T alone. The reconstituted B cell repertoire appeared "naïve" — re-educated without autoimmune memory. An antibody-based trispecific (BCMA×CD19×CD3) attempting to replicate this must achieve comparable depletion depth. The advantage of antibody: no lymphodepletion required, outpatient administration, scalable manufacturing. The risk: antibody may not achieve the same depletion depth as CAR-T; cytokine release syndrome (CRS) risk must be managed.
Disease Biology — SLE as the Lead Indication
SLE (Systemic Lupus Erythematosus) is characterized by pathogenic IgG autoantibodies targeting nuclear antigens (anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-Ro/La). These drive complement activation, immune complex deposition, tissue inflammation, and end-organ damage (particularly lupus nephritis — LN). Both mature B cells (CD19+) and long-lived plasma cells (BCMA+) contribute to the persistent autoantibody load. The type I IFN pathway (targeted by anifrolumab) amplifies B cell autoreactivity. A complete immune reset targeting B cells + plasma cells + T cell-mediated killing would address the root cause of SLE in a way that no existing therapy achieves.
RULE 1 Price moves before readout — market prices in 60–70% by announcement day. Be early or be last. ▾
Read the design, not just the endpoint. A composite estimand inflates remission rates vs. a treatment policy estimand. Duvakitug's 48% Ph2b number may translate very differently in Ph3. Watch estimand choice when sizing expectations.
Primary miss ≠ death. Afimkibart missed Ph2b primary but Roche advanced to Ph3. Pattern: day-of selloff → gradual recovery as secondaries/biomarker data parsed → re-rating when Ph3 is announced with refined population.
p-value ≠ everything. p=0.08 in COPD with a positive eos ≥150 subgroup can still advance; p=0.04 in UC with weak effect size may not. Read magnitude, biomarker enrichment, and estimand choice together.
RULE 2 Upfront % = partner conviction. Upfronts at 6–7% of total for preclinical bispecifics signal real de-risking. ▾
Deal velocity = supply scarcity. Three TL1A×IL-23p19 deals in 12 months (Earendil/Sanofi Apr 2025, Qyuns/Roche Oct 2025, Simcere/BI Jan 2026) signals partners are racing. Next deal in class will likely set a new upfront record.
China rights retention = leverage, not failure. Chinese biotechs retaining Greater China while licensing ex-China is a deliberate strategy that is working. If a company starts licensing including China, it signals urgent cash need or domestic program failure.
Upfront moves stock; biobucks do not. Market discounts milestones 80–90%. A $50M upfront is real money today; $900M in biobucks is mostly hypothetical. Read the upfront, ignore the headline total.
RULE 3 Positive Ph3 lifts the whole class briefly — failure reprices it for 3–6 months. ATLAS-UC (~Nov 2026) is the key watch. ▾
ATLAS-UC positive: Lifts Roche (afimkibart), Sanofi (duvakitug), AZ broadly. Validates bispecific thesis → deal velocity accelerates. Watch for unlicensed asset search to spike.
ATLAS-UC miss: Day-of selloff across TL1A class. Deal appetite freezes 3–6 months. Analyst rewrites on "TL1A class risk" will unfairly tar bispecifics — this is when to be patient. Underlying science doesn't change.
COPD 2026–2027 inflection: Tozorakimab OBERON/MIRANDA, tezepelumab SUNRISE, bosakitug asthma, itepekimab confirmation all reading out. Positive SUNRISE (AZ) would set the bar QX031N must beat — and create a new $10B product.
RULE 4 Chinese bispecific BD window: format advantage + Ph1 HV data required. Window closes as Ph3 data arrives 2026–2027. ▾
Format advantage is the first gate. Monospecific TL1A or TSLP won't command bispecific deal economics. New entrant needs bispecific or long-acting format to compete. Straight monoAb vs. tulisokibart/tezepelumab gets deeply discounted.
SAD/MAD Phase 1 data is the minimum bar. Partners want safety, PK (expected half-life), and biomarker target engagement (TSLP/IL-33 or TL1A suppression). Without Phase 1 human data, deals happen at lower upfronts with high milestone back-loading — "optionality" territory.
The preclinical premium window is ~2–3 more years. After Ph3 IBD data reads out (2026–2027), partners will demand Ph2 POC before paying bispecific premiums. Act now or wait for much higher bar.

📖 Plain English Glossary — Every Term Explained ▸
Disease Area / Pillar
A biological mechanism Ailux has BD interest in — TL1A, TSLP, IL-4Rα, FcRn, IGF1R, T-cell. Every record in the database is tagged to one or more areas. The tabs in the dashboard = areas.
Overlap — Direct / Adjacent / Same-Space
Direct: same target + same patients — head-to-head competition. Adjacent: related mechanism or nearby indication — compared by physicians or in trials. Same-Space: same broad disease area, different enough not to be a direct threat. The most important label in Meridian for BD work.
Enrichment
The automated process that takes a company name + area, gives Claude structured context, and uses its output to fill in drugs, trials, catalysts, and deals. "Enriching UCB" = running the pipeline on UCB for TL1A.
Completeness Score (0–100)
How thoroughly a company/drug has been researched — not how important it is. 0 = not enriched yet. 70+ = strong coverage across all 6 research stages.
Canonical Drug / Canonical ID
One master record per real molecule regardless of how many names it has. "Omvontis" = "RVT-3101" = tulisokibart → one canonical ID. All trials and deals link to that ID, not the name.
Catalyst
A future event that matters for BD — trial readout, FDA filing, conference presentation. Stored with a date. Drives the catalyst timeline on the home page.
Discovery Queue
New companies or drugs Meridian found but hasn't fully researched. Meridian's to-do list for new entities.
drug_area_scores
The database table where Claude's competitive assessments live. One row per drug per area. Stores overlap classification, rationale, vs_ailux positioning. This is the output of enrichment, the input to the dashboard.
Confidence Level — confirmed / supported / inferred
Confirmed: Claude found a direct source. Supported: multiple indirect sources agree. Inferred: Claude reasoned from related evidence. Unverified: claimed but not corroborated. Stored in every record — not yet shown in the UI.
Prompt / Prompt Engineering
The exact instruction text given to Claude. Every classification, summary, and score in Meridian is the output of a specific prompt. Changing the prompt changes all future outputs. The prompts are the most important text in the system.
Supabase
The cloud database where all Meridian data lives. The dashboard reads from it in real time. The enrichment scripts write to it. Think: structured cloud spreadsheet with 20+ linked tables.
Knowledge Graph
Data organized as nodes (company, drug, trial, deal) connected by edges (CONTROLS, TARGETS, PARTNERED_WITH). Unlike a spreadsheet, a graph lets you traverse connections — "which companies that did TL1A deals also have Phase 2 trials?" becomes a traversal, not a manual lookup.
Migration
A versioned change to the database structure — adding a column, creating a new table. Meridian has 21+ migrations applied in order (v1–v21). Each represents a structural capability upgrade.
Terms that still confuse you, definitions that seem wrong
🗄️ How Supabase Organizes Knowledge — The Data Model ▾
Supabase is the structured memory of Meridian. It doesn't store articles or documents — it stores facts in rows and columns, connected by foreign keys (pointers from one table to another). Here is what the structure actually looks like and why it's organized this way.
6-Layer Ontology — Every Level Answers a Unique Question
Layer Industry Term The Question It Answers Examples DB Table
① Therapeutic Area Therapeutic Area Which clinical specialty owns this disease? Gastroenterology · Respiratory · Dermatology · Rheumatology · Neurology · Ophthalmology · Oncology disease_areas
② Indication Indication What disease is being treated? Ulcerative Colitis · Crohn's Disease · Asthma · COPD · Atopic Dermatitis · gMG · TED · Multiple Myeloma indications
③ Biology Tags Subtype / Biology Tag Why does the disease occur? Type 17 · Fibrosis · Autoimmune · Type 2 · Eosinophilic · IGF-1R mediated · B-cell indications.biology_tags[]
④ Target Target What molecule is being manipulated? TL1A · IL-23p19 · TSLP · IL-4Rα · FcRn · IGF-1R · TSHR · BCMA · CD3 targets
⑤ Target Pair Target Pair Which mechanisms are being combined? TL1A × IL-23p19 · IL-23 × α4β7 · TSLP + IL-33 · IGF-1R + TSHR · BCMA × CD3 target_pairs
⑥ Modality Modality How is the target being drugged? mAb · BsAb · TsAb · Small Molecule · ADC · TCE · CAR-T · Fc-fusion · RNA modalities
This terminology matches what biotech BD teams, clinicians, investors, and pharma partners use in practice. Each layer answers a unique question — if two layers answer the same question, they should be merged.

Key Foreign Key Chains — How the Layers Connect
Biology path: disease_areas.id → indications.disease_area → targets.disease_areas[] → target_pairs.target_1/2_id
Entity path: companies.id → company_areas.company_id + area_id → disease_areas.id
Score path: drug_area_scores.(drug_id → drugs.id) + (company_id → companies.id) + (area_id → disease_areas.id)
Event path: catalysts.company_id → companies.id + catalysts.drug_id → drugs.id
Cross-layer bridge: drugs.target (text) → targets.id  ·  drug_targets.target_id → targets.id (normalized)
Classification anchor: ailux_positions (disease_areas.id) → defines Direct/Adjacent/Same-Space → shapes every drug_area_scores row
The key insight: Supabase stores facts, not documents. When you read "cizutamig: Direct competitor in TL1A" on the dashboard, that sentence doesn't exist anywhere in the database. It is assembled on the fly by reading three separate rows — the drug record, the drug_area_scores row, and the company record — and combining them in the browser.
The diagram above also shows a correction to how Meridian originally organized biology. The old disease_areas table listed targets (TL1A, TSLP, FcRn) as if they were the top-level category. That was backwards. Disease areas are IBD, Respiratory, Atopy. Targets are what drugs hit inside those areas. The new schema adds indications (UC, CD, Asthma) as the intermediate layer, and targets as normalized biological entities — so one target like JAK1 can correctly belong to multiple disease areas without duplication.
💡 Why This Structure Matters
Because facts are stored separately and connected by pointers, one fact update fixes the display everywhere at once. If UCB renames a drug, you change one row in drugs and it propagates to every tab, every card, every filter result. And because targets are now normalized rows (not free text), Meridian can answer questions like "which disease areas share a target?" or "what modality is most common in IBD?" — questions that were structurally impossible before.

🔬 A Drug Gets Classified — Full Pipeline Trace ▾
Here is the complete, unabridged sequence of what happens when the enrichment pipeline classifies cizutamig (UCB) as a Direct TL1A competitor. Every step, every query, every piece of data that moves.
1
Pipeline starts — reads the work queue from Supabase
The pipeline reads from tables companies, company_areas, and disease_areas — asking: which companies are tagged to this area and haven't been enriched recently? Companies with status = acquired are excluded (they've been absorbed into another company). The result is sorted so the least-recently-enriched company goes first.
This returns: "UCB, area: TL1A — enriched 3 days ago." UCB moves to the front of the queue because it hasn't been enriched recently.
2
Pipeline fetches everything Meridian already knows about UCB
The pipeline reads everything Meridian already knows about UCB — from tables drugs, drug_area_scores, and catalysts. This existing knowledge gets included in what Claude receives, so Claude builds on prior analysis rather than starting from scratch each time.
This builds the context object — a structured summary of what Meridian already knows. This context gets included in the prompt so Claude doesn't start from scratch.
3
Pipeline calls Claude — Step 3: Drug Discovery
Claude receives a brief about UCB: the company name, disease area focus (TL1A / IBD), which drugs are already in the database, and recent catalysts. Claude is asked to identify all drugs in UCB's TL1A pipeline — name, mechanism, target, clinical stage, and indication. It also assigns a confidence_level to each drug: confirmed if it found a direct source, supported if indirect sources agree, or inferred if it reasoned from available evidence.
Claude returns structured JSON. The pipeline validates it, checks canonical identity (is "cizutamig" already in the database?), then writes each drug as a row in drugs.
4
Pipeline calls Claude again — Step 5: Competitive Classification
Claude receives the drug facts for cizutamig (mechanism: anti-TL1A antibody, phase: Phase 2, indication: Crohn's and UC, company: UCB) along with the full four-tier classification definitions from the ailux_positions table — the exact Direct / Adjacent / Same-Space / Watch criteria shown in the "Definitions" section above. Claude applies those definitions and returns: which tier this drug belongs to, a one-sentence rationale explaining why, a direct comparison to SPY002, and a relevance score from 1–10.
This is the classification call. The exact wording of Direct/Adjacent/Same-Space definitions determines what Claude decides. These words are the most important text in the system.
5
Claude returns a structured conclusion
{
  "overlap": "Direct",
  "overlap_rationale": "cizutamig is an anti-TL1A mAb in Phase 2 for Crohn's and UC — the same target and same patient population as Ailux's bispecific.",
  "vs_ailux_positioning": "Head-to-head competitor. UCB's monospecific vs. Ailux's bispecific will be compared on depth of remission and combo potential.",
  "area_fit": 9,
  "area_fit_rationale": "Core TL1A IBD program — directly relevant to Ailux's space."
}
6
Pipeline writes the conclusion back to Supabase
Claude's output is written into the drug_area_scores table — one row per drug per area. If a score already exists for this drug in this area, it gets overwritten with the new assessment. Fields stored include overlap (the tier), overlap_rationale (the reasoning), vs_ailux (the comparison), and area_fit (a relevance score from 1–10).
The ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE part means: if this drug already has a score for this area, overwrite it. So re-running enrichment updates existing records rather than creating duplicates.
7
Dashboard reads it — and assembles the display
When you open the TL1A tab, the dashboard reads from drug_area_scores, joins it with drugs and companies to get the full picture, filters to area TL1A, and sorts by relevance score — highest first. The "Direct" badge, the rationale text, the comparison note — all come from those stored fields. Nothing is calculated live; it all comes from what Claude wrote during enrichment.
The browser reads this table join and renders the TL1A drug cards. The "Direct" badge, the rationale text, the vs_ailux note — all assembled from those six columns. The HTML you see is built from these rows in real time on every page load.
💡 The Implication
If you change the definition of "Direct" in Step 4's prompt — even one sentence — every future enrichment run will apply the new definition. The old stored scores in Supabase stay as they were. A re-enrichment is needed to update them. This is why the ground truth validation framework exists: you run it after every prompt change to verify the new definition produces the right answers before deploying.

📐 The Definitions That Drive Every Classification ▾
Every drug in Meridian gets classified into one of four tiers. These are the exact definitions Claude reads before making that decision. They live in a database table called ailux_positions — one row per disease area. Changing these definitions changes every future classification. The text below is pulled directly from that table for the IBD / TL1A area.
Ailux's Drug — The Reference Point for Every Classification
Drug: SPY002  ·  Targets: TL1A × IL-23p19  ·  Format: bispecific antibody, subcutaneous  ·  Stage: Phase 2 (UC and CD)
Spyre Therapeutics is developing SPY002, a bispecific antibody that blocks both TL1A (which drives mucosal inflammation in IBD) and IL-23p19 (which drives the Th17 immune pathway). The idea is that blocking both targets in a single injection is more effective than blocking either alone — and more convenient than taking two separate drugs. Ailux's BD strategy is to track and partner around Spyre's competitive position.
Suggest a clearer way to describe Ailux's drug or strategy
Direct Field name stored in database: overlap = "Direct"
What it means: The drug targets TL1A — the same primary target as Ailux — or is a combination program that includes TL1A as one of its components. This is a direct mechanistic threat regardless of what stage the drug is at. Even a preclinical TL1A program counts as Direct.
Real examples: ABBV-701 (AbbVie's anti-TL1A antibody), tulisokibart / MK-7240 (Merck's anti-TL1A), afimkibart / RO7121 (Roche anti-TL1A), duvakitug / SAR447029 (Sanofi anti-TL1A), SIM0709 (BI / Simcere anti-TL1A), and any TL1A × IL-23 bispecific from a competitor company.
Suggest a change to the Direct definition
Adjacent Field name stored in database: overlap = "Adjacent"
What it means: The drug treats IBD (UC or Crohn's) but works through a different mechanism than TL1A. These drugs matter because they either validate the same biology Ailux is working in, or they're being tested as combination partners with TL1A inhibitors. They're not head-to-head competitors — but they shape the treatment landscape that Ailux's drug will enter.
Real examples: Skyrizi / risankizumab (AbbVie's IL-23 blocker, approved for UC and Crohn's), ABBV-382 (AbbVie's α4β7 integrin blocker), vedolizumab / Entyvio (Takeda's α4β7 blocker), mirikizumab / Omvoh (Lilly's IL-23 blocker), ABBV-466 (AbbVie's IL-23 + α4β7 combination program), and any bispecific combining IL-23 with another gut-targeted mechanism.
Suggest a change to the Adjacent definition
Same-Space Field name stored in database: overlap = "Same-Space"
What it means: Approved standard-of-care drugs for IBD that work through a completely different pathway — not TL1A, not IL-23, not α4β7. These drugs treat the same patients Ailux's drug will treat, so they define the efficacy bar that Ailux needs to beat. They're not a mechanistic threat, but they are the commercial benchmark.
Real examples: Ustekinumab / Stelara (J&J's IL-12/23p40 blocker — approved for UC and Crohn's; uses the older, broader p40 target rather than the more selective IL-23p19).
Suggest a change to the Same-Space definition
Watch Field name stored in database: overlap = "Watch"
What it means: IBD drugs with entirely different mechanisms — JAK inhibitors, S1P modulators, TNF inhibitors, RIPK1 inhibitors, and others. These compete for the same patients but through biology unrelated to TL1A or its neighbors. Meridian monitors them for patient-share pressure, safety signals that could affect the whole class, and any signs they're being tested in combination with TL1A drugs.
Real examples: Rinvoq / upadacitinib (AbbVie JAK1), ozanimod (BMS S1P), etrasimod (Pfizer S1P), filgotinib (Galapagos JAK), tofacitinib (Pfizer JAK), TNF inhibitors including Humira, Remicade, and Simponi, lutikizumab (AbbVie IL-1α/β), ABBV-668 (AbbVie RIPK1).
Suggest a change to the Watch definition
What Gets Written About Each Company
For every company in every disease area, Claude writes five specific assessments. These are stored in the database under the company's profile and shown on the dashboard cards. Here is what each one is supposed to capture:
vs_ailux — Mechanism comparison
One or two sentences directly comparing this company's drug to SPY002 — mechanism difference, stage difference, and what that means for competition. For companies not in Ailux's primary areas, this explains why Ailux watches them instead (benchmark value, potential acquirer, cross-area signal). Claude is instructed never to write "no overlap" — there is always a BD reason to monitor.
why_it_matters — BD reason
One or two sentences answering: why does this company matter to Ailux's BD strategy specifically? The answer must be one of: they set a pricing benchmark Ailux should track, they are a potential partner or acquirer, their clinical data validates Ailux's mechanism, or their deal structure defines what counterparties expect. Generic answers are rejected by the prompt.
key_risk — What could go wrong
One or two sentences on the single most important risk for this company's program — trial risk (endpoint design, enrollment problems, regulatory uncertainty), competitive risk (a head-to-head trial coming, a faster competitor), platform risk (the technology itself), or financial risk. Claude is instructed to be specific — not generic summaries.
bd_intelligence.profile — BD behavior classification
Claude classifies each company's dominant BD behavior as one of five types: acquirer (they buy things), licensor (they sell or out-license programs), collaborator (they prefer co-development), partner-friendly (open to deals, history shows it), or internal-focused (they build and keep everything in-house).
platform_intelligence.assessment — Strategic conclusion
A single sentence answering: what does this company's platform trajectory mean for Ailux's competitive positioning or BD timing? For companies in Ailux's primary disease area, this is about competitive threat and timing. For companies in other areas Ailux monitors (FcRn, T-cell, etc.), this is about benchmark value, partnership potential, or cross-area intelligence.

🎛️ How Scoring Works — And How Changing the Prompt Changes the Score ▾
Meridian uses three scoring systems. Each one is an instruction to Claude — not a formula that runs on numbers. Understanding what each prompt asks for makes the scores interpretable. And knowing that the prompt is editable makes the scores improvable.
Score 1: Overlap Classification (Direct / Adjacent / Same-Space)
What the prompt asks
"Given this drug's mechanism and indication, how directly does it compete with Ailux's TL1A bispecific? Use: Direct = same target + same patients, Adjacent = related overlap, Same-Space = shared disease area only."
How to improve accuracy
If a drug is mis-classified, the fix is almost always a clarification to the definition. Example: adding "bispecifics with TL1A as one arm count as Direct" would change how bispecifics are classified without re-running any data pulls.
Score 2: Completeness Score (0–100)
What the scoring checks
Stage 1 — Entity Discovery (10pts): Does this company have a profile entry at all?
Stage 2 — Drug Mapping (15pts): Are drugs linked to this company?
Stage 3 — Trial Intelligence (20pts): Are there ClinicalTrials.gov records for those drugs?
Stage 4 — Catalyst Engine (15pts): Are there upcoming readout dates?
Stage 5 — Strategic Positioning (25pts): Is vs_ailux_positioning written? This is weighted highest because it is the most valuable for BD.
Stage 6 — Deal Intelligence (15pts): Are there deal records?
Key nuance
A score of 0 does not mean bad data — it means the scoring script hasn't processed that entity yet. This was the exact bug found in May 2026: 6 companies showed score=0 but had rich data. The scoring script had simply never been pointed at them. Always check last_scored_at before acting on a low score.

If Stage 5 (Strategic Positioning) matters most to you, you could reweight it from 25pts to 40pts. That would reprioritize the research queue to surface companies missing vs_ailux analysis first.
Score 3: Area Fit (1–10)
What the prompt asks
"On a scale of 1–10, how relevant is this drug to Ailux's TL1A IBD program? 10 = core direct competitor that Ailux must track closely. 1 = only tangentially related to the area."
How it's used
Area fit drives the sort order in the area tabs — drugs with area_fit=9 show first. If you want to see a broader competitive landscape (including drugs you wouldn't normally prioritize), lowering the filter threshold from 7 to 5 would surface more entries. This is a one-line code change in the dashboard.
💡 The Feedback Loop
The ground truth validation framework (28 TL1A test cases) is exactly this loop: change prompt definition → re-run enrichment on test cases → check if known-correct answers still pass → if yes, deploy. Before this framework existed, there was no way to know if a prompt change made things better or worse. Now every change is measurable.

🖥️ How the Dashboard Displays Intelligence — The Filter Chain ▾
When you click the TL1A tab, the dashboard doesn't load a pre-built page — it executes a live chain of database queries, filters the results, and renders what you see in real time. Here is that chain.
TL1A Tab Load Chain
Click
User clicks TL1A tab → JavaScript calls switchTabTo('tl1a') → fires the onEnter() handler registered for that tab
Query 1
Fetch companies in TL1A: company_areas WHERE area_id = tl1a AND status != acquired → returns 18 active companies
Query 2
Fetch drugs with scores: drug_area_scores JOIN drugs WHERE area_id = tl1a AND area_fit >= 7 → returns drug rows with overlap classification already attached
Query 3
Fetch catalysts: catalysts WHERE company_id IN (18 company ids) ORDER BY sort_date → returns upcoming events for those companies
Filter
Browser filters and sorts: drugs grouped by overlap (Direct first, then Adjacent, then Same-Space), sorted by area_fit score descending within each group
Render
JavaScript builds the HTML cards from those rows and injects them into the DOM. The "Direct" badge is a CSS class applied based on the overlap field value.
What this means for what you see: If a drug doesn't appear in the TL1A tab, one of these things is true: (1) it has no row in drug_area_scores for TL1A — enrichment hasn't classified it. (2) It has area_fit < 7 — Claude scored it as low relevance. (3) The company has status = acquired. These are the three filters between a drug existing in the database and appearing in the tab.
💡 Why Things Sometimes Don't Show Up
The most common reason a drug you know about isn't visible in Meridian: it exists in drugs but has no drug_area_scores row for that area. Enrichment runs per company, not per drug. If a company hasn't been enriched for a specific area, its drugs won't appear in that tab even if they clearly belong there.

🕸️ Questions Meridian Can't Answer Yet ▾
These are strategic BD questions that the current data model cannot compute directly — not because the information doesn't exist, but because the right connections between records haven't been built yet. Each one is one missing relationship away from being answerable.
"Which drugs directly compete with Ailux's TL1A bispecific?" Blocked
Overlap classification exists per drug, but there's no drug → COMPETES_WITH → drug edge. You can see that two drugs are both "Direct" competitors, but the system can't directly link them. Fix: one migration + backfill from existing drug_area_scores. Highest leverage, lowest effort.
"Which mechanism class is most crowded for TL1A?" Blocked
Drug targets are stored as free text ("TL1A", "BCMA×CD3"). "Which drugs share TL1A as target" requires a text search, not a database join. Fix: a targets table where each target is a proper node with a drug→TARGETS→target relationship.
"Which deal brought this drug into this company's portfolio?" Partially blocked
Ownership records exist, deal records exist — but there's no FK linking them. You can see UCB controls cizutamig (Phase 1) and you can see the UCB/Candid acquisition deal, but the system doesn't know they're connected.
"Which company's competitive position changed most in the last 6 months?" Needs delta view
Ownership records have dates, but there's no query that diffs snapshots over time. Cannot auto-surface "UCB went from 0 to 4 TL1A assets in 90 days."
"What did Company X present at DDW this year?" No conference data
No conference nodes, no abstract/poster records, no presentation-to-drug links. Conference data is completely absent from the graph despite being the highest-value early signal source.
💡 Did you know
The top 3 missing relationships by leverage vs. effort: (1) drug→COMPETES_WITH→drug — can be backfilled from data already in the DB. (2) targets table — normalizes free text into queryable nodes. (3) ownership_edges.deal_id FK — closes the provenance chain. Any of these would unlock a class of queries that currently require manual reasoning.

🏠 Home Page — What You're Seeing & What's Missing ▾
The home page has four information panels. Each one pulls from a different part of the database — here's exactly what logic drives each one and where its current limitations are.
📅 Catalysts & Signals
Pulls from catalysts table sorted by upcoming date. Covers ~595 deduplicated events. Limitation: entries are only as current as the last enrichment run — there's no real-time monitoring. Conference dates are included but without abstract content.
💼 Deal Activity
Pulls from deals table filtered by area, with accordion cards and Google News links. Deduplication applied client-side (60% keyword overlap threshold). Limitation: deals are discovered reactively through company enrichment, not from a dedicated deal-monitoring feed.
⚡ Essential Updates
Pulls from intel table. Limitation: intel is not being refreshed from live sources — no Fierce Biotech, no Endpoints. What you see is what the enrichment script discovered, which may be days or weeks behind.
🔬 Research Queue
Shows entities ranked by enrichment priority score. Useful for directing manual research effort. Limitation: the scoring only captures completeness (how researched), not strategic importance (how much to care). A thin company with low BD relevance ranks the same as a thin company you should urgently study.
💡 Did you know
The Meridian Issue (📰 button) is a separate AI-generated daily briefing — it runs as a separate workflow and produces a structured narrative digest. It's distinct from the live database panels. If the issue looks stale, the workflow may not have run — check GitHub Actions.

🎛️ Every Filter, Category & Sort — The Full Control Panel ▸
Every lever in the dashboard — every filter chip, dropdown, sort column, and classification bucket — is listed here. The terms below are the same terms used in the database. If you see "Direct" on a drug card, that value came from drug_area_scores.overlap = 'Direct'. If you see "Phase 3" on a filter pill, the data field is drugs.stage. The dashboard is a view over the database, not a separate system.
⬡ Cross-Cutting Classification Systems
These four dimensions are applied across every drug on every area tab. They are the primary sorting, filtering, and visual-encoding axes in the dashboard.
OVERLAP drug_area_scores.overlap · Controls row color, sort position, and visual tier on area pipeline tables
Direct
Same target + same indication + direct mechanism overlap with Ailux — the core competitive set
Adjacent
Same area, different mechanism or indication — competes for the same patient or deal
Same-Space
Same disease area, overlapping biology but not head-to-head — context for the landscape
Watch
Early signal — mechanism or company worth monitoring before formal competitive relevance
Sort order: Direct → Adjacent → Same-Space → Watch (controlled by OV_ORDER constant)
CLASS drugs.class · Generation of mechanism — how far from the original biology
1st Gen
First-generation mechanism — original proof of biology (e.g., first anti-TL1A mAbs)
2nd Gen
Optimized mechanism — improved dosing, half-life, selectivity, or formulation
Next Gen
Novel mechanism — bispecific, combination, or platform differentiation from first-gen
Sort order: Next Gen → 2nd Gen → 1st Gen (highest-differentiation first when sorting by Class)
STAGE drugs.stage · Clinical development phase — filter chips on every area tab and DKN
Approved BLA Filed Phase 3 Phase 2/3 Phase 2 Phase 1/2 Phase 1b Phase 1 Preclinical
Sort order: Approved(0) → BLA Filed(0.5) → Phase 3(1) → Phase 2/3(1.5) → Phase 2(2) → Phase 1/2(2.5) → Phase 1b(2.8) → Phase 1(3) → Preclinical(5)
ENTITY TYPE companies.entity_type · What kind of company this is
standalone platform partnership licensed

🧬 Ontology Reference — How Biology Is Organized
The biology hierarchy controls how everything maps to areas. The dashboard speaks in disease area tabs; the database thinks in Disease Area → Indication → Target → Target Pair. This is the translation layer.
Level Examples DB Table Dashboard Role
Disease Area IBD · Respiratory · Atopy · TED · Autoimmune · T-cell disease_areas Tab structure on the dashboard. Each tab = one or more area_ids.
Indication UC · CD · Asthma · COPD · AD · CSU · TED · gMG · CIDP · MM · ALL indications Indication dropdown in DKN. Bridge between area and target.
Target TL1A · IL-23p19 · TSLP · IL-33 · IL-4Rα · FcRn · IGF-1R · TSHR targets Target area chips in DKN. Drug mechanism labeling.
Target Pair TL1A×IL-23p19 · TSLP+IL-33 · IL-4Rα×TSLP · IGF-1R+TSHR · BCMA×CD3 target_pairs DKN target area chips. Classification anchor for Next Gen bispecifics.
Modality Reference
mAb Monoclonal antibody · BsAb Bispecific antibody · TsAb Trispecific antibody · SM Small molecule · ADC Antibody-drug conjugate · VHH Nanobody · TCE T-cell engager · CAR-T CAR-T cell therapy · Fc-fusion Fc-fusion protein · RNA RNA therapeutic
